en.title: Foreign Minister Shahid sends National Day greetings to Foreign Minister of Romania
en.description: Foreign Minister Shahid sends National Day greetings to Foreign Minister of Romania
en.body:
Foreign Minister Shahid sends National Day greetings to Foreign Minister of Romania

The Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Maldives, Abdulla Shahid sends a message of felicitations to Bogdan Aurescu, Minister of Foreign Affairs of Romania, on the occasion of the National day of Romania.

Minister’s message reads as follows:

“On behalf of the Government, the people of the Republic of Maldives and on my own behalf, it gives me great pleasure to extend warm greetings and good wishes to Your Excellency, the Government and the people of Romania, on the occasion of National Day.

It is my sincere hope that the friendly relations that exist between our two countries will continue to prosper in the days ahead.

Please accept, Excellency, the assurances of my highest consideration.”

en.title: High Commissioner of Maldives to Malaysia His Excellency Ali Hussain Didi presents his Letter of Credence to His Majesty the Yang di-Pertuan Agong
en.description: High Commissioner of Maldives to Malaysia His Excellency Ali Hussain Didi presents his Letter of Credence to His Majesty the Yang di-Pertuan Agong
en.body:
High Commissioner of Maldives to Malaysia His Excellency Ali Hussain Didi presents his Letter of Credence to His Majesty the Yang di-Pertuan Agong

The High Commissioner of the Republic of Maldives to Malaysia, His Excellency Ali Hussain Didi presented his credentials to His Majesty the Yang di-Pertuan Agong XVI, Al-Sultan Abdullah Ri'ayatuddin Al-Mustafa Billah Shah ibni Almarhum Sultan Haji Ahmad Shah Al-Musta'in Billah on Thursday, 1 December 2022 at Istana Negara, Kuala Lumpur.

The High Commissioner was received in audience by His Majesty the King following the submission of Credentials. During the audience, the High Commissioner conveyed best wishes from His Excellency Ibrahim Mohamed Solih, President of the Republic of Maldives to His Majesty the King for his good health and happiness as well as for peace, prosperity and happiness of the people of Malaysia. The King congratulated the High Commissioner on his appointment and assured full support and cooperation from the Government of Malaysia in discharging his responsibilities in his capacity as High Commissioner of the Republic of Maldives to Malaysia.

The High Commissioner conveyed his gratitude to the people and Government of Malaysia for their support to the Maldives, as we continue to strengthen the friendly relations between both countries.

The High Commissioner was accompanied by his spouse Ms. Aishath Juman and, Deputy High Commissioner Uza. Mariyam Mizna Shareef.

en.title: Minister Shahid sends greetings on the occasion of the 55th anniversary of diplomatic ties between Maldives and the Republic of Korea
en.description: Minister Shahid sends greetings on the occasion of the 55th anniversary of diplomatic ties between Maldives and the Republic of Korea
en.body:
Minister Shahid sends greetings on the occasion of the 55th anniversary of diplomatic ties between Maldives and the Republic of Korea

The Minister of Foreign Affairs of Maldives, His Excellency Abdulla Shahid has sent a message of felicitation to His Excellency Park Jin, Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea, on the 55th Anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic relations between the Republic of Maldives and the Republic of Korea.

Minister’s message reads as follows:

“ It gives me great pleasure to extend my sincere greetings to Your Excellency, the Government, and the people of the Republic of Korea, on the prestigious occasion of the 55th Anniversary of the establishment of Diplomatic Relations between Maldives and the Republic of Korea.

During the 55 years of bilateral relations, the bonds of close partnership between our two nations, founded on mutual respect and trust, common values and ideology, have prospered significantly over the past years, leaving the Republic of Korea close to the hearts of many Maldivian people.

I am confident that the historical ties and enduring friendship will be further strengthened with constructive engagements in areas of mutual benefit for both countries.

As we mark this important milestone in our bilateral relations, I wish to convey to Your Excellency, the Government, and the people of the Republic of Korea continued success, peace, and prosperity.

Please accept, Excellency, the assurances of my highest consideration. ”

en.title: Ceremony held to handover US$ 100 million financial assistance from the Government of India to the Government of Maldives
en.description: Ceremony held to handover US$ 100 million financial assistance from the Government of India to the Government of Maldives
en.body:
Ceremony held to handover US$ 100 million financial assistance from the Government of India to the Government of Maldives

The Government of India handed over a financial assistance of US$ 100 million to the Government of Maldives, amid the economic challenges faced by the Maldives, in a ceremony held at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs today.

At the ceremony, a symbolic cheque was handed over by the High Commissioner of India, Munu Mahawar on behalf of the Government of India, to the Minister of Foreign Affairs Abdulla Shahid on behalf of the Government of Maldives. This financial support of US$ 100 million to the Government of Maldives will be provided through subscription in Maldives’ Government Domestic Treasury bonds by SBI, Malè.

Speaking at the event, Minister Shahid highlighted the effectiveness of President Solih’s far-sighted foreign policy in building the trust and confidence in Maldives for the international community. Furthermore, Minister Shahid reflected on the significance of the historically close ties between the Maldives and India in providing crucial assistance in the progress and development of the Maldives.

The ceremony was attended by Minister of Finance, Ibrahim Ameer who also delivered a statement. Minister of External Affairs of India, Dr. S. Jaishankar also participated in the ceremony via direct videoconferencing and delivered his remarks virtually.

In addition, members of Parliament, High Commissioners, senior officials from the Ministry of Finance, High Commission of India in Maldives and the State Bank of India also attended the ceremony.

en.title: The newly appointed High Commissioner of Pakistan to the Maldives calls on Foreign Minister Shahid
en.description: The newly appointed High Commissioner of Pakistan to the Maldives calls on Foreign Minister Shahid
en.body:
The newly appointed High Commissioner of Pakistan to the Maldives calls on Foreign Minister Shahid

The newly appointed High Commissioner of Pakistan to the Maldives, Vice Admiral (Rtd) Muhammad Fayyaz Gilani paid a courtesy call on the Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Maldives, Abdulla Shahid, today.

During the meeting Minister Shahid welcomed the High Commissioner and congratulated him on presenting credentials as the High Commissioner of Pakistan in the Maldives. The Minister further noted the excellent bonds of friendship that exist between the two nations, and exchanged views with the High Commissioner on ways to further deepen bilateral cooperation and collaboration.

High Commissioner Gilani thanked the Minister for the warm welcome and expressed his commitment to work closely with the Government and the people of Maldives to further strengthen the friendship between the two countries.

Minister Shahid was accompanied by Secretary Bilateral, Dr Hala Hameed, Additional Secretary, Ibrahim Uvais and Assistant Director, Aishath Fareena.

en.title: Newly appointed High Commissioner of Singapore to the Maldives pays a courtesy call on Foreign Minister
en.description: Newly appointed High Commissioner of Singapore to the Maldives pays a courtesy call on Foreign Minister
en.body:
Newly appointed High Commissioner of Singapore to the Maldives pays a courtesy call on Foreign Minister

The newly appointed High Commissioner of Singapore to the Maldives, His Excellency Soo Kok Leng, paid a courtesy call on the Minister of Foreign Affairs, His Excellency Abdulla Shahid, this afternoon.

During the meeting, Minister Shahid congratulated High Commissioner Soo on his appointment and expressed confidence that the long-standing ties between the two countries will be further strengthened during his tenure.

Minister Shahid stated that the Maldives attaches great importance to its relations with Singapore and appreciates the continued assistance and cooperation received from Singapore towards the development of Maldives. Both Minister Shahid and High Commissioner Soo also exchanged views to further enhance cooperation between the two countries. High Commissioner Soo assured Singapore will continue to provide technical assistance towards the socio-economic development of the Maldives.

Minister Shahid was accompanied by Secretary Bilateral at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs Dr. Hala Hameed, Additional Secretary Amin Javed Faizal, and Assistant Director Ibrahim Haail.

High Commissioner Soo was accompanied by Ms. Roshni Sharma, Country Officer (South Asia & Sub-Saharan Africa Directorate) at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Singapore.

en.title: Foreign Minister Shahid meets with USAID Deputy Assistant Administrator Kaur
en.description: Foreign Minister Shahid meets with USAID Deputy Assistant Administrator Kaur
en.body:
Foreign Minister Shahid meets with USAID Deputy Assistant Administrator Kaur

The Minister of Foreign Affairs of Maldives, Abdulla Shahid met the Deputy Assistant Administrator of the Bureau for Asia at the United States Agency for International Development (USAID) Änjali Kaur, this morning.

During the meeting held at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Minister Shahid and Deputy Assistant Administrator Kaur discussed the growing partnership between the Maldives and USAID, especially in the areas of public finance management, democratic governance, individual and community resilience and the environment.

Both Minister Shahid and Deputy Assistant Administrator Kaur further reflected on the ongoing projects of USAID in the Maldives and explored potential avenues to expand the partnership. Minister Shahid also expressed appreciation to USAID and the Government of the United States for the continuous contributions made towards the socio-economic development of the Maldives and stressed on the importance of sustaining the partnership.

Minister Shahid was accompanied by Minister of State for Foreign Affairs Ahmed Khaleel, Secretary (Bilateral) Dr. Hala Hameed, Joint Secretary Shiuneen Rasheed and Assistant Director Mohamed Shaffau Ibrahim.

Deputy Assistant Administrator Kaur was accompanied by USAID Mission Director Gabriel Grau and officials from the USAID Mission to the Maldives.

en.title: Maldives and the United States sign the ninth amendment to the Development Objective Grant Agreement (DOAG)
en.description: Maldives and the United States sign the ninth amendment to the Development Objective Grant Agreement (DOAG)
en.body:
Maldives and the United States sign the ninth amendment to the Development Objective Grant Agreement (DOAG)

The ninth amendment to the Development Objective Grant Agreement (DOAG) has been signed between the Maldives and the United States of America, today.

During a ceremony held at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Minister of State for Foreign Affairs Ahmed Khaleel signed the ninth amendment to the DOAG on behalf of the Government of the Republic of Maldives. On behalf of the Government of the United States of America, USAID Mission Director Gabriel Grau signed the agreement.

The DOAG is a landmark development cooperation agreement signed between the Maldives and the United States, on 12 March 2019. To date, eight amendments have been brought to this agreement, bringing the total contribution from the United States to USD 25.94 million. Through the ninth amendment concluded today, the United States Government commits an additional USD 3 million to the Maldives, to improve Maldives’ technical capacity to manage public finances and improve the resilience of Maldives’ economic and democratic governance.

The signing ceremony of the ninth amendment of the DOAG was witnessed by senior officials from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, USAID Deputy Assistant Administrator for the Bureau of Asia, and officials from USAID Mission to the Maldives.

en.title: The New High Commissioner of Maldives to India Presents Credentials to the President of India
en.description: The New High Commissioner of Maldives to India Presents Credentials to the President of India
en.body:
The New High Commissioner of Maldives to India Presents Credentials to the President of India

The newly appointed High Commissioner of the Republic of Maldives to the Republic of India, His Excellency Ibrahim Shaheeb, presented his Letter of Credence to Her Excellency Droupadi Murmu, President of the Republic of India, at a ceremony held at Rashtrapati Bhavan today.

During the courtesy call held following the ceremony, High Commissioner Shaheeb conveyed greetings from His Excellency President Ibrahim Mohamed Solih, the Government and the People of the Republic of Maldives to the President and the friendly people of India. High Commissioner Shaheeb further expressed appreciation for the support received from India in the socio-economic development of Maldives and conveyed commitment to work closely with the Government of India and its people, with a renewed focus on taking the relationship to new heights especially expanding trade and investment ties between the two countries. President Murmu congratulated High Commissioner on his appointment and expressed hope to work closely with the Maldives in further strengthening the bilateral relations between the two countries in areas of mutual interest.

Today’s ceremony was witnessed by the Spouse of High Commissioner, Madam Mariyam Ilham Niyaz. In addition, Defence Advisor of Maldives in India, Col. Mohamed Ibrahim, First Secretary, Mr. Ahmed Suzil, First Secretary, Ms. Maryam Bassam Farooq, and Second Secretary, Mr. Nuaz Afeef from the High Commission of Maldives in India participated in the event.

President Ibrahim Mohamed Solih appointed His Excellency Ibrahim Shaheeb as the High Commissioner of the Republic of Maldives to the Republic of India on 10 October 2022.

en.title: Foreign Minister Shahid meets with Foreign Minister of UAE
en.description: Foreign Minister Shahid meets with Foreign Minister of UAE
en.body:
Foreign Minister Shahid meets with Foreign Minister of UAE

Foreign Minister His Excellency Abdulla Shahid, the Special Envoy of President His Excellency Ibrahim Mohamed Solih has met with the Minister of Foreign Affairs of the United Arab Emirates, His Highness Sheikh Abdulla bin Zayed Al Nahyan.   At the meeting held at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of UAE, Minister Shahid handed over a letter from President Solih addressed to His Highness Sheikh Mohammed bin Zayed Al Nahyan, President of the United Arab Emirates, and conveyed greetings and well wishes from President Solih to the leadership and the Emirati people.   During the meeting, the Ministers conversed on ways to further strengthen and diversify the long-standing relations between the Maldives and UAE. Minister Shahid reiterated appreciation for the generous support and assistance provided to the Maldives through the Abu Dhabi Fund for Development, and expressed gratitude on behalf of the government and people of the Maldives for the invaluable contributions made by UAE towards the socio-economic development of the Maldives, over the years.   The two Foreign Ministers expressed their renewed commitment to working together on issues of mutual interest, both bilaterally and in the international fora.   Foreign Minister Shahid was accompanied at the meeting by the Ambassador of the Republic of Maldives to the United Arab Emirates, Her Excellency Aminath Shabeena, Assistant Director at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Ahmed Salman Zaki and Second Secretary of the Embassy of the Republic of Maldives in the United Arab Emirates, Fathimath Urooj Nizar.

en.title: State Minister Ahmed Khaleel attends the 22nd IORA Meeting of the Council of Ministers
en.description: State Minister Ahmed Khaleel attends the 22nd IORA Meeting of the Council of Ministers
en.body:
State Minister Ahmed Khaleel attends the 22nd IORA Meeting of the Council of Ministers

Minister of State for Foreign Affairs His Excellency Ahmed Khaleel today participated in the 22nd Meeting of the Council of Ministers of the Indian Ocean Rim Association (IORA) held in Dhaka, Bangladesh. The meeting held under the theme “Harnessing the opportunities of the Indian Ocean sustainably for inclusive development” was hosted by the current Chair of IORA, the People's Republic of Bangladesh.

The meeting brought together Ministers from the 23 Member States of IORA in which they reiterated their commitment to “supporting IORA to play a significant role in promoting sustainable and inclusive development in the Indian Ocean through constructive dialogue and concerted efforts as well as to address challenges and key issues in collaboration with Dialogue Partners”. The Dhaka Communiqué was adopted at the end of the meeting.

In his statement to the Council of Ministers, State Minister Khaleel drew attention to the risks and exposure that Small Island Developing States face due to the effects of climate change. He also called upon Member States to share experiences and technologies, pass knowledge and to work together to protect the environment of the Indian Ocean.

State Minister Khaleel further noted the firm commitment of the Maldives to the common principles enshrined in the IORA Charter and called on Member States to revive the true spirit of regional cooperation.

State Minister Ahmed Khaleel was accompanied by Her Excellency Shiruzimath Sameer, High Commissioner of Maldives to the People’s Republic of Bangladesh; Ms. Mariyam Reesha, Director General, Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Mr. Ali Firushan, Deputy Desk Officer, Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

IORA is a leading inter-governmental organization formed in 1997 to enhance regional and socio-economic cooperation and development among the Indian Ocean Region countries. The Maldives formally joined IORA on 8 November 2019, as its 22nd Member State. The 22nd Council of Ministers meeting was preceded by the 24th Committee of Senior Officials meeting that took place in Dhaka from 22-23 November 2022.

en.title: Foreign Minister Shahid engages with UN Country Team
en.description: Foreign Minister Shahid engages with UN Country Team
en.body:
Foreign Minister Shahid engages with UN Country Team

The Minister of Foreign Affairs Abdulla Shahid met with the United Nations Country Team today, during their annual retreat.

During the interaction, the Minister shared his experience as the President of the United Nations General Assembly, noting the important role country teams needs to play in translating what is happening in New York to the local level, help connect the various processes, and find opportunities for projects and examples from the national level, to be featured in events and processes globally.

The Minister also thanked the UN Country team led by the UN Resident Coordinator for the dedication, commitment and for supporting the development path of the Government of Maldives.

The Minister requested UN Country Team to discuss ways to enhance coordination and work together towards the implementation of the United Nations Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework (UNSDCF) 2022-2026.

The Minister was accompanied by Joint Secretary Mariyam Midhfa Naeem, Assistant Director Aishath Shahula, and Assistant Director Ahmed Salman Zaki.

dv.body:
އ.ދ.ގެ ސަލާމަތީ މަޖިލީހާއި އ.ދ.ގެ އިކޮނޮމިކް އެންޑް ސޯޝަލް ކައުންސިލްގެ މެމްބަރު ޤައުމަކަށް ވުމަށް ދިވެހިރާއްޖެއިން ކުރިމަތިލާން ނިންމައިފި

އ.ދ.ގެ މައި ދެ ގުނަވަން ކަމުގައިވާ އ.ދ.ގެ ސަލާމަތީ މަޖިލީހާއި އ.ދ.ގެ އިކޮނޮމިކް އެންޑް ސޯޝަލް ކައުންސިލްގެ މެމްބަރު ޤައުމަކަށް ވުމަށް ދިވެހިރާއްޖެއިން ކުރިމަތިލާން ނިންމައިފިއެވެ. އެގޮތުން އ.ދ.ގެ ސަލާމަތީ މަޖިލީހަށް ކުރިމަތިލާން ނިންމާފައިވަނީ 2033-2034 ގެ ޓަރމްއަށެވެ. އަދި އ.ދ.ގެ އިކޮނޮމިކް އެންޑް ސޯޝަލް ކައުންސިލްއަށް ކުރިމަތިލާން ނިންމާފައިވަނީ 2027-2029 ޓަރމްއަށެވެ. މި އިންތިޚާބުތައް ދިވެހިރާއްޖެ ކާމިޔާބު ކޮށްފިނަމަ، އެކަން ވާނީ މި ދެ ގުނަވަނަށްވެސް ދިވެހިރާއްޖެއިން އިންތިޚާބުވާ ފުރަތަމަ ފަހަރަށެވެ.

ދިވެހިރާއްޖެއާއި ދޭދޭ ޤައުމުތަކާއި ބައިނަލްއަޤްވާމީ ޖަމިއްޔާތަކާ އޮންނަ ގުޅުން ހަރުދަނާކޮށް ބައިނަލްއަޤްވާމީ މައިދާނުގައި ރާއްޖޭގެ ހަރަކާތްތެރިކަން އިތުރު ކުރުމަކީ ސަރުކާރުގެ ވައުދެކެވެ. ހަމައެހެންމެ، ބައިނަލްއަޤްވާމީ މައިދާނުގައި ދިވެހިރާއްޖޭގެ އެންމެ މަތީ މަސްލަހަތު ކުރިއަރުވައި، ދިވެހިރާއްޖެއަށް ރީތި ނަން ހޯދުމަކީވެސް ސަރުކާރުގެ ވައުދެކެވެ. މި އިންތިޚާބުތަކުގައި ވާދަކުރުމަށް ދިވެހި ސަރުކާރުން ނިންމާފައިވަނީ މި ވައުދުތަކަށް ބިނާކޮށް، ޤައުމަށް އަލިގަދަ މުސްތަގްބަލެއް ހޯދުމުގެ މަޤްސަދުގައެވެ. މިގޮތުން، 2018 އިން ފެށިގެން ހޯދާފައިވާ ކާމިޔާބުތަކުގެ ތެރޭގައި، އ.ދ.ގެ އާންމު މަޖިލީހުގެ ރިޔާސަތު ބެލެހެއްޓުމާއި އ.ދ.ގެ އިންސާނީ ހައްގުތަކާ ބެހޭ ކައުންސިލަށް އިންތިޚާބުވުން ހިމެނެއެވެ. މިހާތަނަށް ދިވެހިރާއްޖެއިން ހޯދާފައިވާ ކާމިޔާބުތަކަކީ ކުދި ޖަޒީރާ ޤައުމުތަކުން ބައިނަލްއަޤްވާމީ މައިދާނުގައި މުހިންމު ދައުރެއް އަދާ ކުރެވޭނެ ކަމުގެ އަލިގަދަ ދަލީލެކެވެ.

އ.ދ.ގެ ސަލާމަތީ މަޖިލީހުގެ މައިގަނޑު މަޤްސަދަކީ ބައިނަލްއަޤްވާމީ ސަލާމަތާއި ރައްކާތެރިކަން ޤާއިމްކުރުމެވެ. އަދި އ.ދ.ގެ އިކޮނޮމިކް އެންޑް ސޯޝަލް ކައުންސިލްގެ މައިގަނޑު މަޤްސަދަކީ ދެމެހެއްޓެނިވި ތަރައްޤީގެ ލަނޑުދަނޑިތައް ހާސިލްކުރުމަށް ޤައުމުތަކަށް އެހީތެރިކަން ފޯރުކޮށްދިނުމެވެ.

dv.title: އ.ދ.ގެ ސަލާމަތީ މަޖިލީހާއި އ.ދ.ގެ އިކޮނޮމިކް އެންޑް ސޯޝަލް ކައުންސިލްގެ މެމްބަރު ޤައުމަކަށް ވުމަށް ދިވެހިރާއްޖެއިން ކުރިމަތިލާން ނިންމައިފި
dv.description: އ.ދ.ގެ ސަލާމަތީ މަޖިލީހާއި އ.ދ.ގެ އިކޮނޮމިކް އެންޑް ސޯޝަލް ކައުންސިލްގެ މެމްބަރު ޤައުމަކަށް ވުމަށް ދިވެހިރާއްޖެއިން ކުރިމަތިލާން ނިންމައިފި
dv.body:
އ.ދ.ގެ ސަލާމަތީ މަޖިލީހާއި އ.ދ.ގެ އިކޮނޮމިކް އެންޑް ސޯޝަލް ކައުންސިލްގެ މެމްބަރު ޤައުމަކަށް ވުމަށް ދިވެހިރާއްޖެއިން ކުރިމަތިލާން ނިންމައިފި

އ.ދ.ގެ މައި ދެ ގުނަވަން ކަމުގައިވާ އ.ދ.ގެ ސަލާމަތީ މަޖިލީހާއި އ.ދ.ގެ އިކޮނޮމިކް އެންޑް ސޯޝަލް ކައުންސިލްގެ މެމްބަރު ޤައުމަކަށް ވުމަށް ދިވެހިރާއްޖެއިން ކުރިމަތިލާން ނިންމައިފިއެވެ. އެގޮތުން އ.ދ.ގެ ސަލާމަތީ މަޖިލީހަށް ކުރިމަތިލާން ނިންމާފައިވަނީ 2033-2034 ގެ ޓަރމްއަށެވެ. އަދި އ.ދ.ގެ އިކޮނޮމިކް އެންޑް ސޯޝަލް ކައުންސިލްއަށް ކުރިމަތިލާން ނިންމާފައިވަނީ 2027-2029 ޓަރމްއަށެވެ. މި އިންތިޚާބުތައް ދިވެހިރާއްޖެ ކާމިޔާބު ކޮށްފިނަމަ، އެކަން ވާނީ މި ދެ ގުނަވަނަށްވެސް ދިވެހިރާއްޖެއިން އިންތިޚާބުވާ ފުރަތަމަ ފަހަރަށެވެ.

ދިވެހިރާއްޖެއާއި ދޭދޭ ޤައުމުތަކާއި ބައިނަލްއަޤްވާމީ ޖަމިއްޔާތަކާ އޮންނަ ގުޅުން ހަރުދަނާކޮށް ބައިނަލްއަޤްވާމީ މައިދާނުގައި ރާއްޖޭގެ ހަރަކާތްތެރިކަން އިތުރު ކުރުމަކީ ސަރުކާރުގެ ވައުދެކެވެ. ހަމައެހެންމެ، ބައިނަލްއަޤްވާމީ މައިދާނުގައި ދިވެހިރާއްޖޭގެ އެންމެ މަތީ މަސްލަހަތު ކުރިއަރުވައި، ދިވެހިރާއްޖެއަށް ރީތި ނަން ހޯދުމަކީވެސް ސަރުކާރުގެ ވައުދެކެވެ. މި އިންތިޚާބުތަކުގައި ވާދަކުރުމަށް ދިވެހި ސަރުކާރުން ނިންމާފައިވަނީ މި ވައުދުތަކަށް ބިނާކޮށް، ޤައުމަށް އަލިގަދަ މުސްތަގްބަލެއް ހޯދުމުގެ މަޤްސަދުގައެވެ. މިގޮތުން، 2018 އިން ފެށިގެން ހޯދާފައިވާ ކާމިޔާބުތަކުގެ ތެރޭގައި، އ.ދ.ގެ އާންމު މަޖިލީހުގެ ރިޔާސަތު ބެލެހެއްޓުމާއި އ.ދ.ގެ އިންސާނީ ހައްގުތަކާ ބެހޭ ކައުންސިލަށް އިންތިޚާބުވުން ހިމެނެއެވެ. މިހާތަނަށް ދިވެހިރާއްޖެއިން ހޯދާފައިވާ ކާމިޔާބުތަކަކީ ކުދި ޖަޒީރާ ޤައުމުތަކުން ބައިނަލްއަޤްވާމީ މައިދާނުގައި މުހިންމު ދައުރެއް އަދާ ކުރެވޭނެ ކަމުގެ އަލިގަދަ ދަލީލެކެވެ.

އ.ދ.ގެ ސަލާމަތީ މަޖިލީހުގެ މައިގަނޑު މަޤްސަދަކީ ބައިނަލްއަޤްވާމީ ސަލާމަތާއި ރައްކާތެރިކަން ޤާއިމްކުރުމެވެ. އަދި އ.ދ.ގެ އިކޮނޮމިކް އެންޑް ސޯޝަލް ކައުންސިލްގެ މައިގަނޑު މަޤްސަދަކީ ދެމެހެއްޓެނިވި ތަރައްޤީގެ ލަނޑުދަނޑިތައް ހާސިލްކުރުމަށް ޤައުމުތަކަށް އެހީތެރިކަން ފޯރުކޮށްދިނުމެވެ.

en.title: Newly appointed Ambassador of the Dominican Republic to the Maldives calls on Foreign Minister Shahid
en.description: Newly appointed Ambassador of the Dominican Republic to the Maldives calls on Foreign Minister Shahid
en.body:
Newly appointed Ambassador of the Dominican Republic to the Maldives calls on Foreign Minister Shahid

The newly appointed Ambassador of the Dominican Republic to the Maldives, David Puig, made a courtesy call on the Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Maldives, Abdulla Shahid, today.

During the meeting held at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Minister Shahid congratulated Ambassador Puig on his appointment and discussed avenues for strengthening bilateral relations between the two countries in areas of mutual importance such as visa facilitation, and environment and climate change. Minister Shahid and Ambassador Puig also reassured commitment to enhance cooperation in the multilateral arena.

Minister Shahid was accompanied by Secretary Bilateral Dr. Hala Hameed, Joint Secretary Shiuneen Rasheed, and Desk Officer Saifulla Waleed.

en.title: Newly appointed Ambassador of Netherlands to the Maldives calls on Foreign Minister Shahid
en.description: Newly appointed Ambassador of Netherlands to the Maldives calls on Foreign Minister Shahid
en.body:
Newly appointed Ambassador of Netherlands to the Maldives calls on Foreign Minister Shahid

The newly appointed Ambassador of Netherlands to the Maldives, Bonnie Horbach, made a courtesy call on Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Maldives, Abdulla Shahid, this afternoon.

During the meeting, Minister Shahid congratulated Ambassador Horbach on her appointment and highlighted on the longstanding relations that exist between the Maldives and the Netherlands. Both Minister Shahid and Ambassador Horbach also exchanged views to further enhance cooperation between the two countries, especially in the areas of environment and climate change. Minister Shahid and Ambassador Horbach also reaffirmed their commitment to continue working closely in the multilateral arena.

Minister Shahid was accompanied by Secretary Bilateral Dr. Hala Hameed, Joint Secretary Shiuneen Rasheed and Assistant Director Mohamed Shaffau Ibrahim.

en.title: Maldives and EU to hold the Sixth Policy Dialogue
en.description: Maldives and EU to hold the Sixth Policy Dialogue
en.body:
Maldives and EU to hold the Sixth Policy Dialogue

The Government of the Maldives will host the Sixth Maldives-EU Policy Dialogue on Wednesday, 23 November 2022. The purpose of this annual dialogue is to facilitate open and constructive engagement between the Maldives and the European Union (EU) to further strengthen the existing ties of friendship and cooperation between the Maldives and the EU.

This year’s dialogue will include discussions on democracy, governance and strengthening of the justice sector, security cooperation, trade, tourism, investment, finance and economic cooperation, environment and climate change and Schengen Visa facilitation.

The EU delegation will be led by the Ambassador of the European Union to the Maldives, Denis Chaibi. The Maldives Delegation will be led by Minister of Foreign Affairs, Abdulla Shahid. Ambassadors of the European Union and senior officials of the Maldivian Government will also participate in the dialogue.

en.title: Minister Shahid sends Independence Day greetings to Lebanon
en.description: Minister Shahid sends Independence Day greetings to Lebanon
en.body:
Minister Shahid sends Independence Day greetings to Lebanon

The Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Maldives, Abdulla Shahid sends a message of felicitations to Abdallah Bouhabib, Minister of Foreign Affairs and Emigrants of the Lebanese Republic, on the occasion of Lebanon’s Independence Day.

Minister’s message reads as follows:

“It is my pleasure to extend greetings and good wishes to Your Excellency, the Government, and the people of Lebanon on the festive occasion of the Lebanese Independence Day.

Please accept my sincere good wishes for Your Excellency’s good health and wellbeing and continued prosperity for the people of Lebanon. I am confident that the friendly relations between our two countries will grow stronger in the years ahead.

Please accept, Excellency, the assurances of my highest consideration.”

en.description: Maldives to put forward candidatures to the United Nations Security Council and the United Nations Economic and Social Council
en.body:
Maldives to put forward candidatures to the United Nations Security Council and the United Nations Economic and Social Council

The Government of Maldives has decided to put forward its candidatures for membership as a non-permanent member of the United Nations Security Council for the term 2033-2034, and for membership of the United Nations Economic and Social Council, for the term 2027-2029. If successful, it would be the first time Maldives becomes a member of both principal organs of the United Nations (UN).

The decision to contest in both elections stems from the commitment of the Government of Maldives towards strong international engagement in the multilateral arena, as a responsible member of the international community. Since 2018, Maldives has successfully competed for elections to the Presidency of the seventy-sixth session of the UN General Assembly, and the United Nations Human Rights Council, for the term 2023-2025. Despite small island developing States (SIDS) like Maldives being under-represented across the UN, Maldives has consistently demonstrated that even the smallest of countries can make meaningful contributions at the highest levels of decision-making. The Government of Maldives is confident in the country’s ability to significantly contribute towards global discourse on international peace and security and sustainable development.

The Security Council is the principal organ of the UN mandated with the maintenance of international peace and security. It is also the highest decision-making body in the international system. The Economic and Social Council is the principal organ of the UN mandated with the implementation of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) as well as the coordination, policy review and the formulation of recommendations on all economic, social and environmental matters.

en.title: Newly appointed Non-Resident Ambassador of Algeria to Maldives calls on the Minister of Foreign Affairs
en.description: Newly appointed Non-Resident Ambassador of Algeria to Maldives calls on the Minister of Foreign Affairs
en.body:
Newly appointed Non-Resident Ambassador of Algeria to Maldives calls on the Minister of Foreign Affairs

The newly appointed Non-Resident Ambassador of the People’s Democratic Republic of Algeria to the Republic of Maldives, Abderrahmane Benguerrah has paid a courtesy call on the Minister of Foreign Affairs, Abdulla Shahid, today.

During the meeting held at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Minister Shahid welcomed Ambassador and congratulated him on presenting credentials as the Non-Resident Ambassador of Algeria. Highlighting the long-standing bilateral relations between the Maldives and Algeria, Minister Shahid and Ambassador Benguerrah exchanged ideas to further deepen the bilateral ties, cultural exchanges and people-to-people contact between the two countries.

Ambassador Benguerrah thanked the Minister for the warm welcome, and conveyed his strong commitment to working closely with the Government and people of the Maldives to further enhance collaborations between the two countries.

Minister Shahid was accompanied by Secretary Bilateral Dr. Hala Hameed, Director Moomina Ibrahim and Senior Desk Officer Aminath Abdulla.

en.title: Director General of the National Centre for Good Governance of India, Mr. Bharat Lal, calls on Minister of Foreign Affairs
en.description: Director General of the National Centre for Good Governance of India, Mr. Bharat Lal, calls on Minister of Foreign Affairs
en.body:
Director General of the National Centre for Good Governance of India, Mr. Bharat Lal, calls on Minister of Foreign Affairs

The Director General of the National Centre for Good Governance (NCGG) of India, Mr. Bharat Lal called on Minister of Foreign Affairs, Abdulla Shahid today at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

Minister Shahid welcomed NCGG Director General Bharat Lal to the Maldives and shed light on the strong bilateral relationship between the Maldives and India, highlighting its beneficial contribution towards enhancing human resource development in the Maldives. Referring to the MoU signed between the Civil Service Commission of the Maldives and the NCGG, Minister Shahid extended his appreciation to the Government of India for delivering numerous capacity building programmes as a means to strengthening the capability and efficiency of the civil servants across government institutions of the Maldives. Minister Shahid concluded the meeting by expressing his hope that these capacity-building programmes will gradually increase in number and expand the people-to-people connections between the Maldives and India.

Director General Bharat Lal is on an Official Visit to the Maldives hosted by the President of the Civil Service Commission of the Maldives, from 18 to 22 November 2022.

en.title: Foreign Minister Shahid sends a message of good wishes and congratulations to the Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister of Qatar
en.description: Foreign Minister Shahid sends a message of good wishes and congratulations to the Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister of Qatar
en.body:
Foreign Minister Shahid sends a message of good wishes and congratulations to the Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister of Qatar

The Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Maldives, Abdulla Shahid sends a message of good wishes and congratulations to Mohammed bin Abdulrahman bin Jassim Al Thani, Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs of the State of Qatar, on the eve of the opening of the 2022 FIFA World Cup.

Minister’s message reads as follows:

“It gives me great pleasure to send good wishes and warm congratulations to Your Excellency, the Government and the people of Qatar, on the eve of the opening of the 2022 FIFA World Cup.

It is a matter of immense pride that Qatar is the first Muslim country, and only the second Asian country to host the World Cup. As a small State, the Maldives is also extremely proud of the fact that Qatar is the smallest country to host the World Cup - a fact that demonstrates the capability and ability of small States to make meaningful contributions in every field.

We congratulate the Qatari people for the excellent preparations for the World Cup, especially during a time of recovery from a global pandemic. And we applaud the Government’s efforts to enhance sustainability during the World Cup, including in energy use, waste management, and infrastructure.

The people of the Maldives looks forward to an entertaining and successful 2022 World Cup, and wish the people of Qatar every success.

Please accept, the assurances of my highest considerations.”

en.title: Foreign Minister Shahid sends National Day greetings to Foreign Minister of Monaco
en.description: Foreign Minister Shahid sends National Day greetings to Foreign Minister of Monaco
en.body:
Foreign Minister Shahid sends National Day greetings to Foreign Minister of Monaco

The Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Maldives, Abdulla Shahid sends a message of felicitations to Isabelle Berro Amadei, Minister of Foreign Affairs and Cooperation of the Principality of Monaco, on the occasion of the National day of Monaco.

Minister’s message reads as follows:

“It gives me great pleasure to extend warm greetings and best wishes to Your Excellency, the Government and the people of Monaco, on the joyous occasion of your National Day.

I look forward to working with Your Excellency to further enhance our cooperation both in the bilateral and multilateral spheres for the mutual benefit of our two countries

I also extend best wishes for your good health and well-being, and for further progress of the people of the Principality of Monaco.

Please accept, the assurances of my highest considerations.”

en.title: Minister Shahid sends National Day greetings to Oman
en.description: Minister Shahid sends National Day greetings to Oman
en.body:
Minister Shahid sends National Day greetings to Oman

The Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Maldives, Abdulla Shahid sends a message of felicitations to Sayyid Badr bin Hamad bin Hamood Albusaidi, Foreign Minister of the Sultanate of Oman, on the occasion of Oman’s National Day.

Minister’s message reads as follows:

“It is my pleasure to extend greetings and good wishes to Your Excellency, the Government, and the people of Oman on the jubilant occasion of Oman’s National Day.

I remain assured that the bilateral relations between our nations rooted in links of history and culture, and shared Islamic values, will grow from strength to strength in the days ahead.

Please accept, Excellency, the assurances of my highest consideration.”

en.title: Foreign Minister Shahid sends Independence Day greetings to the Foreign Minister of Latvia
en.description: Foreign Minister Shahid sends Independence Day greetings to the Foreign Minister of Latvia
en.body:
Foreign Minister Shahid sends Independence Day greetings to the Foreign Minister of Latvia

The Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Maldives, Abdulla Shahid sends a message of felicitations to Edgars Rinkēvičs, Minister of Foreign Affairs of Latvia, on the occasion of the Independence Day of Latvia.

Minister’s message reads as follows:

“On behalf of the Government, the people of the Republic of Maldives and on my own behalf, it gives me great pleasure to extend warm greetings and best wishes to Your Excellency, the Government and the people of Latvia, on the occasion of your Independence Day.

I am confident that the friendly relations between our two countries as well as our cooperation in both bilateral and multilateral spheres will continue to thrive in the years to come.

Please accept, Excellency, the assurances of my highest consideration.”

en.title: Minister Shahid sends Independence Day greetings to Palestine
en.description: Minister Shahid sends Independence Day greetings to Palestine
en.body:
Minister Shahid sends Independence Day greetings to Palestine

The Minister of Foreign Affairs of Maldives, Abdulla Shahid sends a message of felicitations to Riad Al Malki, Minister for Foreign Affairs of Palestine, on the occasion of the Independence Day of the State of Palestine.

Minister’s message reads as follows:

“It is my pleasure to extend warm felicitations and good wishes to Your Excellency, the Government and the brotherly people of the State of Palestine, on the occasion of your Independence Day.

Let me take this opportunity to reaffirm the solidarity we share with the people and the Government of Palestine and reiterate our steadfast commitment to advocate for the cause of Palestine within the international community.

I hope that the close ties between our two nations strengthen in the days ahead.

Please accept, Excellency, the assurances of my highest consideration.”

en.title: Minister Shahid meets with Special Envoy of the Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea
en.description: Minister Shahid meets with Special Envoy of the Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea
en.body:
Minister Shahid meets with Special Envoy of the Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea

Minister of Foreign Affairs Abdulla Shahid, met with the Special Envoy of the Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea and Ambassador at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea, Han Dongman, today. The Special Envoy is currently undertaking a visit to the Maldives from 13 – 14 November 2022.

During the meeting held this morning, the Minister Shahid welcomed the Special Envoy to the Maldives and noted that this visit would serve to further strengthen the bilateral relations between the Maldives and the Republic of Korea, as 2022 marks the 55th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic relations between the two countries.

Minister Shahid expressed his appreciation for the generous contributions of the Government of the Republic of Korea, including through agencies such as the Korea International Cooperation Agency (KOICA), to the development of the Maldives. He also expressed his eagerness to see the expansion of relations between the two countries in the fields of economic and technical cooperation.

Minister Shahid was accompanied by the Minister of State for Foreign Affairs Ahmed Khaleel, Additional Secretary (Asia, Middle East, and Africa Department) Amin Javed Faizal, Joint Secretary (Multilateral Department) Mariyam Midhfa Naeem, and Assistant Director (Multilateral Department) Fathimath Zeyna Abdulla Saeed.

The Special Envoy is accompanied by the Ambassador of the Republic of Korea to the Maldives, Woonjin Jeong, and other senior officials. During the visit, the Special Envoy also called on the Speaker of the People’s Majlis President Mohamed Nasheed, Minister for Economic Development Uz. Fayyaz Ismail, and the Minister of Tourism Dr. Abdulla Mausoom.

en.title: Newly appointed Australian High Commissioner to the Maldives calls on Foreign Minister Shahid
en.description: Newly appointed Australian High Commissioner to the Maldives calls on Foreign Minister Shahid
en.body:
Newly appointed Australian High Commissioner to the Maldives calls on Foreign Minister Shahid

The newly appointed Australian High Commissioner to the Maldives, Paul Stephens, made a courtesy call on the Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Maldives, Abdulla Shahid, this afternoon.

During the meeting held at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Minister Shahid congratulated High Commissioner Stephens on his appointment and discussed on the longstanding relations between the two countries in a wide range of areas. Both Minister and High Commissioner further expressed hope that the close cooperation, especially in the fields of education, security, environment and climate change, would expand with the opening of a new resident High Commission of Australia in Maldives. Minister Shahid and High Commissioner Stephens also reassured commitment to enhance cooperation on multilateral issues of mutual importance.

Minister Shahid was accompanied by Secretary Bilateral Dr. Hala Hameed, Joint Secretary Shiuneen Rasheed, and Assistant Director Mohamed Shaffau Ibrahim.

en.title: Minister Shahid sends greetings on the occasion of the 55th anniversary of diplomatic ties between Maldives and Japan
en.description: Minister Shahid sends greetings on the occasion of the 55th anniversary of diplomatic ties between Maldives and Japan.
en.body:
Minister Shahid sends greetings on the occasion of the 55th anniversary of diplomatic ties between Maldives and Japan.

The Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Maldives, Abdulla Shahid has sent a message of felicitation to Hayashi Yoshimasa, Minister of Foreign Affairs of Japan, on the 55th Anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic relations between the Republic of Maldives and Japan.

Minister’s message reads as follows:

"It gives me great pleasure to convey warm greetings and sincere good wishes of the Government and the people of Maldives, and those of my own, to Your Excellency, the Government, and the friendly people of Japan, as we celebrate the 55th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic relations between the Maldives and Japan.

Over these 55 years, our bilateral relations have maintained sound and steady growth and have stood the test of time. Our partnership has grown to encompass many areas of cooperation notably the contribution towards the socio-economic development of Maldives. Today, our countries continue to enjoy excellent and multifaceted relations, which are underpinned by strong bonds of friendship and expanding people-to-people exchanges.

Looking ahead, we are confident that what we have accomplished within the last five decades has been mutually beneficial for both our peoples and remain assured that the best years of our partnership are still ahead of us.

Please accept, Excellency, my best wishes for your success, good health and well-being and for the peace, progress and prosperity of the people of Japan."

en.title: Minister Shahid sends a message of condolence to the Foreign Minister of Egypt
en.description: Minister Shahid sends a message of condolence to the Foreign Minister of Egypt
en.body:
Minister Shahid sends a message of condolence to the Foreign Minister of Egypt

The Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Maldives, Abdulla Shahid has sent a message of condolence to the Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Arab Republic of Egypt, Sameh Hassan Shoukry Selim following the loss of lives in a tragic mini bus crash in the city of Dekahliye, Egypt, on 12 November 2022.

Minister’s message reads as follows:

“I was deeply shocked and saddened to learn of the tragic news of the mini bus crash in the city of Dekahliye, Egypt, on 12 November 2022, causing the loss of lives of more than 20 people and injuring many.

At this time of distress, the Government and the people of Maldives join me in extending our deepest condolences to Your Excellency, the Government and the people of Egypt. Our sincere prayers are with the bereaved families, and we wish for the quick and complete recovery of the injured.

Please accept, Excellency, the assurances of my highest consideration.”

en.title: Minister Shahid sends Independence Day Greetings to Angola
en.description: Minister Shahid sends Independence Day Greetings to Angola
en.body:
Minister Shahid sends Independence Day Greetings to Angola

The Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Maldives, Abdulla Shahid sends a message of felicitations to the Minister for External Relations of the Republic of Angola, Téte António, on the occasion of the Independence Day of Angola. Minister’s message reads as follows:

“It is my pleasure to extend greetings and good wishes to Your Excellency, the Government, and the people of Angola on the joyous occasion of Angola’s Independence Day.

I am confident that the bilateral ties between our two nations would continue to flourish in the days to come.

Let me also convey my best wishes for peace, progress and prosperity to the people of Angola.

Please accept, Excellency, the assurances of my highest consideration.”

dv.title: މިނިސްޓަރ އޮފް ފޮރިން އެފެއާޒް އިންޑިއާގެ އެކްސްޓަރނަލް އެފެއާޒް މިނިސްޓަރާއި ބަންގްލަދޭޝްގެ ފޮރިން މިނިސްޓަރާ ފޯނުން ގުޅުއްވައި ތަޢުޒިޔާ ވިދާޅުވެއްޖެ
dv.body:
ތަޢުޒިޔާ ވިދާޅުވުން

މިނިސްޓަރ އޮފް ފޮރިން އެފެއާޒް ޢަބްދުﷲ ޝާހިދު، އިންޑިއާގެ އެކްސްޓަރނަލް އެފެއާޒް މިނިސްޓަރ ޑރ ޖައިޝަންކަރާއި ބަންގްލަދޭޝްގެ ފޮރިން މިނިސްޓަރު ޑރ އޭ.ކޭ. ޢަބްދުލް މޮމެން އާ ފޯނުން ގުޅުއްވައި މިއަދު މާލޭގައި ހިނގައިދިޔަ އަލިފާނުގެ ހިތާމަވެރި ހާދިސާގައި އެ ދެ ޤައުމުގެ ރައްޔިތުން ނިޔާވުމާ ގުޅިގެން ތަޢުޒިޔާ ވިދާޅުވެއްޖެއެވެ. މިނިސްޓަރުގެ ވާހަކަފުޅުގައި ދިވެހި ރައްޔިތުންނާއި ދިވެހި ސަރުކާރުގެ ނަމުގައި މި ހާދިސާގައި ނިޔާވި އެ ޤައުމުތަކުގެ ރައްޔިތުންގެ އާއިލާތަކަށް ތަޢުޒިޔާ ރައްދުކޮށްދެއްވުމަށް އެދިވަޑައިގަތެވެ. ހަމައެއާއެކު، މި ހާދިސާ ހިނގައިދިޔަ ގޮތުގެ ފުރިހަމަ ތަޙުގީގެއް ކުރަމުންދާ ވާހަކައާއި މިހާތަނަށް ލިބިފައިވާ މަޢުލޫމާތު ހިއްސާ ކުރެއްވިއެވެ. އަދި މި އުނދަގޫ ދަނޑިވަޅުގައި ދިވެހި ސަރުކާރުގެ ފުރިހަމަ އެހީއާއި އެއްބާރުލުން އެ ދެ ޤައުމުގެ ހައިކޮމިޝަން މެދުވެރިކޮށް، ލިބިގެންދާނެކަމުގެ ފުރިހަމަ ޔަގީންކަން ދެއްވިއެވެ.

en.title: Non-Resident Ambassador of Maldives to Laos presents Credentials to the President of the Lao People’s Democratic Republic
en.description: Non-Resident Ambassador of Maldives to Laos presents Credentials to the President of the Lao People’s Democratic Republic
en.body:
Non-Resident Ambassador of Maldives to Laos presents Credentials to the President of the Lao People’s Democratic Republic

The Non-Resident Ambassador of Republic of Maldives to the Lao People’s Democratic Republic, His Excellency Mohamed Jinah presented his Letter of Credence to the President of the Lao People’s Democratic Republic His Excellency Mr. Thongloun Sisoulith, at a ceremony held this afternoon at the Presidential Palace, Vientiane.

During the brief courtesy call following the Credentials Ceremony, Ambassador Jinah expressed his gratitude for being given the honour to present his Letter of Credence and serve as the Non-Resident Ambassador of Maldives to Laos. Ambassador Jinah also conveyed greetings from His Excellency President Ibrahim Mohamed Solih and the people of Maldives to the President and People of Laos. Ambassador Jinah further expressed commitment to work closely with the Laos Government with a renewed focus in enhancing the bilateral relationship, and also focusing in the areas of promoting tourism, trade, and other areas of mutual interest. The President of Laos congratulated Ambassador Jinah on the assumption of his duties as Non-Resident Ambassador of Maldives to Laos and expressed hope to work closely with the Maldives in further strengthening the bilateral relations and increase people to people to contact between the two countries.

During his visit to Laos, Ambassador Jinah also paid courtesy calls on a number of senior dignitaries at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs including His Excellency Phoxay Khaykhamphithoune, Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs to discuss further on exploring opportunities and enhancing the cooperation between the two countries.

en.title: JOINT PRESS STATEMENT - Official visit to the Maldives by His Excellency Péter Szijjártó, Minister of Foreign Affairs and Trade of Hungary
en.description: Official visit to the Maldives by His Excellency Péter Szijjártó, Minister of Foreign Affairs and Trade of Hungary
en.body:
Official visit to the Maldives by His Excellency Péter Szijjártó, Minister of Foreign Affairs and Trade of Hungary

The Minister of Foreign Affairs and Trade of the Republic of Hungary, Péter Szijjártó, paid an official visit to the Maldives on 9 November 2022, on the invitation of the Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Maldives, Abdulla Shahid. Minister Szijjártó was accompanied by an official delegation from the Government of Hungary.

During this visit, Minister Szijjártó paid a courtesy call on the President of the Republic of Maldives, Ibrahim Mohamed Solih. Minister Shahid and Minister Szijjártó also held Official talks and key agreements were signed to further strengthen the existing bilateral relations between Maldives and Hungary. Minister Szijjártó further held meetings with the Minister of Economic Development, Uz. Fayyaz Ismail and the Minister of Higher Education, Dr. Ibrahim Hassan.

At the Official talks, both the Ministers explored avenues to enhance cooperation especially in the fields of trade, health, education, youth and sports, fisheries, tourism, environment, and climate change. Underscoring the importance of enhancing trade and investment between the two countries, both the Ministers signed an agreement to promote business linkages, exchange of expertise and convene seminars between Maldives and Hungary. Under this agreement, a Joint Economic Commission comprising of officials and experts from both the countries will also be established to guide the development of projects, activities and programmes related to the agreement.

On cooperation in the field of higher education, Minister of Higher Education of the Maldives, Dr. Ibrahim Hassan, and Minister Szijjártó, signed an additional protocol to the Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) concluded between the Maldives and Hungary in 2021 regarding the Stipendium Hungaricum scholarship programme. The additional protocol to the existing MoU would provide a total of 25 scholarships annually which is an increase of 10 scholarships, to Maldivian students to study bachelors, masters and doctoral level courses from Universities in Hungary.

Minister of Youth, Sports and Community Empowerment of the Maldives, Ahmed Mahloof and Minister Szijjártó, also signed an MoU in the field of sports diplomacy with the interest to establish and develop close cooperation in this area. The MoU would facilitate organisation of sports events, exchange of expertise in sports infrastructure and provide training opportunities.

Recalling the importance of enhancing people-to-people ties between the two countries, Minister Szijjártó announced the Government of Hungary’s decision to join the VFS Visa facilitation Centre in Male and to commence operations in November 2022. Minister Shahid expressed appreciation for this decision and reiterated the Government of Maldives interest to obtain visa free status for Maldivian nationals to travel to EU member states.

Minister Shahid also expressed appreciation for the support provided by the Government of Hungary during his presidency at the 76th session of the United Nations General Assembly and reaffirmed the support of the Government of Maldives to Ambassador Kőrösi as the President of the 77th session of the United Nations General Assembly. Minister Szijjártó also congratulated the Maldives on being elected to the UN Human Rights Council for the term 2023-2025 and expressed commitment to enhance engagement within the multilateral sphere to tackle global challenges of mutual interest.

On regional and international issues of mutual importance, Minister Shahid reiterated his appreciation to the Government of Hungary for their assistance in facilitating safe passage for Maldivian students in Ukraine via Hungary in March this year. Minister Shahid also commended the Government of Hungary for their key role in providing the necessary humanitarian assistance regarding the ongoing conflict in Europe.

The visit of Foreign Minister Szijjártó marks the first-ever official visit to Maldives by a Foreign Minister of Hungary.

en.title: Minister of Foreign Affairs and Trade of Hungary arrives in the Maldives on an Official visit
en.description: Minister of Foreign Affairs and Trade of Hungary arrives in the Maldives on an Official visit
en.body:
Minister of Foreign Affairs and Trade of Hungary arrives in the Maldives on an Official visit

The Minister of Foreign Affairs and Trade of Hungary, His Excellency Péter Szijjártó has arrived in the Maldives today, on an Official visit, on the invitation of the Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Maldives, His Excellency Abdulla Shahid.

During this visit, Minister Szijjártó will pay a courtesy call on the President of the Republic of Maldives His Excellency Ibrahim Mohamed Solih. Minister Szijjártó will also hold Official Talks with Minister Shahid, and sign three agreements between Maldives and Hungary.

This is the first Official visit from a Minister of Foreign Affairs and Trade of Hungary and marks an important milestone in the 47 year long bilateral relationship between the Maldives and Hungary.

en.title: Minister Shahid sends Independence Day greetings to Cambodia
en.description: Minister Shahid sends Independence Day greetings to Cambodia
en.body:
Minister Shahid sends Independence Day greetings to Cambodia

The Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Maldives, His Excellency Abdulla Shahid has sent a message of felicitation to the Deputy Prime Minister, Minister for Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation of the Kingdom of Cambodia, His Excellency Mr. Prak Sokhonn, on the occasion of the 69th Independence Day of Cambodia.

Minister’s message reads as follows:

“It gives me great pleasure to extend warm greetings and good wishes to Your Excellency and the people of the Kingdom of Cambodia on the occasion of the 69th Anniversary of Independence.

I look forward to working closely with your Excellency in deepening our friendship, strengthening our ties, and broadening our cooperation based on our shared values.

Let me also take this opportunity to extend my best wishes to Your Excellency’s good health and success, and for the continued peace, progress, and prosperity of the people of the Kingdom of Cambodia. Please accept, Excellency, the assurances of my highest consideration."

en.title: Minister of Foreign Affairs and Trade of Hungary concludes Official visit to the Maldives
en.description: Minister of Foreign Affairs and Trade of Hungary concludes Official visit to the Maldives
en.body:
Minister of Foreign Affairs and Trade of Hungary concludes Official visit to the Maldives

The Minister of Foreign Affairs and Trade of Hungary, His Excellency Péter Szijjártó has concluded his Official visit to the Maldives.

Minister Szijjártó was seen-off at the Velana International Airport by Minister of Foreign Affairs His Excellency Abdulla Shahid and senior officials from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

During this visit, Minister Szijjártó made a courtesy call on the President of the Republic of Maldives, His Excellency Ibrahim Mohamed Solih and held bilateral meetings with the Minister of Higher Education, Dr. Ibrahim Hassan and Minister of Economic Development, Uz. Fayyaz Ismail. Minister Shahid and Minister Szijjártó also held Official talks and three agreements were signed to further strengthen the existing bilateral relations between Maldives and Hungary.

This was the first Official visit by a Foreign Minister from Hungary to the Maldives.

The Minister of Foreign Affairs and Trade of Hungary, His Excellency Péter Szijjártó will make an official visit to the Maldives on 9 November 2022, on the invitation of the Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Maldives, Abdulla Shahid.

During this visit, Minister Szijjártó will pay a courtesy call on the President of the Republic of Maldives, Ibrahim Mohamed Solih. Minister Szijjártó will also hold official talks with his counterpart Abdulla Shahid, Minister of Foreign Affairs, and sign a number of key agreements between Maldives and Hungary.

This visit will mark the first ever official visit to the Maldives by a Hungarian Foreign Minister.

en.title: Foreign Minister concludes official visit to the Republic of Serbia
en.description: Foreign Minister concludes official visit to the Republic of Serbia
en.body:
Foreign Minister concludes official visit to the Republic of Serbia

Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Maldives, Abdulla Shahid concludes the Official Visit to Serbia today. Minister Shahid undertook this visit at the invitation of his counterpart, First Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs of Serbia, Ivica Dačić.

During the visit, Minister Shahid held bilateral discussions with Minister Dačić where the Ministers reviewed the existing relationship between the two countries and explored avenues to further enhance cooperation. The discussions concluded with the signing of a Memorandum of Understanding on Bilateral Political Consultations between the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Maldives and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Serbia.

Minister Shahid also met with Speaker of the National Assembly of the Republic of Serbia, Vladimir Orlić. They discussed the important role of parliaments to strengthen and promote democracy and enhance cooperation between the Maldives and Serbia.

en.title: Foreign Minister Shahid meets the First Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Serbia
en.description: Foreign Minister Shahid meets the First Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Serbia
en.body:
Foreign Minister Shahid meets the First Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Serbia

Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Maldives, Abdulla Shahid has met with the First Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Serbia, His Excellency Ivica Dačić, this morning.

During the meeting, the Ministers had constructive discussions on enhancing the existing bilateral relations in a multitude of areas, such as education cooporation, youth development, health, and tourism. In this regard, Serbia informed that they are ready to receive 20 to 25 young sportspersons between the ages 12 to 18 from the Maldives to train them in volleyball, football and handball. This initiative is expected to be realised by mid 2023. Additionally, the Serbian Government is also willing to increase the scholarships they offer to Maldivian students.

Minister Shahid also raised the possibility of establishing a visa waiver agreement between the Maldives and Serbia. Minister noted that such an agreement would increase people to people ties, promote tourism and add to the bilateral portfolio between Maldives and Serbia. This request will be taken into consideration by the Government of Serbia.

The meeting was followed by the signing of a Memorandum of Understanding on bilateral political consultation. The MoU aims to deepen Maldives’ and Serbia’s political engagement by having periodic consultations to enhance cooperation on areas of mutual interest.

Minister Shahid is currently on an official visit to Belgrade on the invitation of his counterpart, Minister Dačić.

en.title: Foreign Minister Shahid concludes official visit to the United Kingdom
en.description: Foreign Minister Shahid concludes official visit to the United Kingdom
en.body:
Foreign Minister Shahid concludes official visit to the United Kingdom

Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Maldives, Abdulla Shahid concludes the Official Visit to United Kingdom today. The purpose of the visit was to engage with the new leadership of the Government of the United Kingdom to reaffirm the commitment of the Maldives to foster the existing close relationship, and discuss and explore additional areas for cooperation. Minister Shahid also addressed the youth at the Oxford Union Society on the future of multilateralism.

During the visit, Minister Shahid met with the Secretary of State for Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Affairs of the UK, The Rt. Hon. James Cleverly. The Ministers reviewed the existing bilateral portfolio between the two countries and explored avenues to further enhance cooperation especially on obtaining duty free access to the UK, for fish and fish products from the Maldives.

Minister Shahid also met senior officials of the Government including the Minister of State for the Middle East, South Asia and the United Nations at the Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office and the Prime Minister’s Special Representative for Preventing Sexual Violence in Conflict, Lord Tariq Ahmad of Wimbledon, Minister for Asia, Energy, Climate and Environment, The Rt. Hon. Lord Goldsmith and Minister for Development at the Foreign Commonwealth and Development Office, The Rt. Hon. Andrew Mitchell, MP, Deputy Chairman of the Commonwealth Enterprise and Investment Council (CWEIC), Sir Hugo Swire, co-chairs of the Maldives All Party Parliamentary Group (APPS) Lord Bilimoria and Yasmin Qureshi MP, and several other members of the British parliament.

During his address at the Oxford Union, Minister Shahid stated that at a time when the effectiveness of the multilateral system is called into question, we cannot forget that no country, no matter how powerful, can survive unilaterally. He reiterated that we cannot forgo multilateralism as it is the only system that gives everyone an equal voice, that lets problems and solutions be contextualized, is inclusive of all communities and the only system under which we can preserve an increasingly fragile and precious global peace. He called to endeavor to build a United Nations 2.0 as envisioned in the Secretary General’s Our Common Agenda – a United Nations that is more inclusive and responsive to the needs of communities; one whose General Assembly commands more moral authority; and one whose Security Council is more inclusive where veto privileges are not abused.

Maldives and United Kingdom have a long history of close relations since the establishment of diplomatic relations between the two countries on 26 July 1965. The United Kingdom is an invaluable development partner of the Maldives, and the two countries cooperate on numerous areas including counter terrorism and violent extremism, tourism, trade, higher education and climate change and environment.

Minister’s message reads as follows:

en.title: Foreign Secretary meets with Executive Secretary of UN ESCAP
en.description: Foreign Secretary meets with Executive Secretary of UN ESCAP
en.body:
Foreign Secretary meets with Executive Secretary of UN ESCAP

Foreign Secretary Ahmed Latheef, met with the Executive Secretary of the UN Economic and Social Commission for Asia and the Pacific (ESCAP), Under-Secretary-General Armida Salsiah Alisjahbana, today. The Executive Secretary of ESCAP currently undertaking a visit to the Maldives from 29 – 31 October 2022.

During the meeting held this morning, the Foreign Secretary welcomed the Executive Secretary to the Maldives and noted that this visit would tremendously help efforts to attain the Sustainable Development Goals in the Maldives.

He expressed his appreciation to the Executive Secretary for co-organizing an event on Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and the Role of the Parliament with the Government of Maldives, the United Nations Resident Coordinator for the Maldives, United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) and the Inter-parliamentary Union (IPU). The event aims to offer parliamentarians in the Maldives an overview of the 2030 Agenda and the 17 SDGs and the challenges in the Asia-Pacific region and the Maldives, the role of the parliament in advancing the SDGs.

Foreign Secretary was accompanied by the Permanent Representative of Maldives to UN-ESCAP Huda Shareef, Joint Secretary (Multilateral Department) Mariyam Midhfa Naeem, and Assistant Director (Multilateral Department) Fathimath Zeyna Abdulla Saeed.

ESCAP is the most inclusive intergovernmental platform in the Asia and the Pacific. The ESCAP Secretariat supports inclusive, resilient and sustainable development in the region by generating action-oriented knowledge, and by providing technical assistance and capacity building services in support of national development objectives, regional agreements, and the implementation of the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development. ESCAP also provides support to partners at the national level.

en.title: Maldives to host the "Third Maldives – European Union Senior Officials meeting
en.description: Maldives to host the "Third Maldives – European Union Senior Officials meeting
en.body:
Maldives to host the "Third Maldives – European Union Senior Officials meeting

The Third Maldives – European Union Senior Officials meeting will be held at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs this afternoon. The Senior Officials Meeting between the Maldives and the European Union is held annually to facilitate open and constructive engagement between the Maldives and the European Union and to further strengthen the existing ties of friendship and cooperation between the sides.

The thematic areas of discussion of this years meeting will be on Governance, Democracy, Human Rights, Rule of Law; Prevention of Violent Extremism and Counterterrorism, Economic and Trade Cooperation, Development Cooperation; sectoral issues; regional cooperation and international cooperation.

The Maldives delegation will be led by Minister of State for Foreign Affairs Ahmed Khaleel. Senior officials from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, the President’s Office, Ministry of Defence, Ministry of Economic Development, Ministry of Environment, Climate Change and Technology, Ministry of Fisheries, Marine Resources and Agriculture, Attorney General’s Office, National Security Advisor’s Office, Maldives Police Service and National Counter Terrorism Center will participate in this meeting.

The delegation from the European Union will be led by the Deputy Managing Director at the European External Action Service, Paola Pampaloni.

High Commissioner of Maldives to Singapore His Excellency Ahmed Thasmeen Ali presents his Letter of Credence to the President of Singapore Her Excellency Madam

The newly appointed High Commissioner of the Republic of Maldives to the Republic of Singapore, His Excellency Mr. Ahmed Thasmeen Ali, presented his Letter of Credence to the President of the Republic of Singapore, Her Excellency Madam Halimah Yacob at the official ceremony held this morning at the Office of the President of the Republic of Singapore – Istana.

Following the ceremony, Madam President Halimah Yacob and High Commissioner Thasmeen exchanged greetings and good wishes, while acknowledging the close cordial relations that exist between the two countries.

High Commissioner Thasmeen conveyed greetings and good wishes from His Excellency President Ibrahim Mohamed Solih and the people of the Republic of Maldives to Madam President Halimah Yacob and the friendly people of Singapore.

High Commissioner Thasmeen thanked Madam President Halimah Yacob for accepting his credential and reassured his commitment and support to further enhance and elevate the existing long-standing friendly ties between the two countries to new heights during his tenure.

High Commissioner Thasmeen was accompanied at the ceremony by his spouse Madam Visam Ali and, Ms. Aishath Jumana, Second Secretary at the High Commission of Maldives in Singapore.

President Ibrahim Mohamed Solih appointed His Excellency Mr. Ahmed Thasmeen Ali as the High Commissioner of the Republic of Maldives to the Republic of Singapore on 25th August 2022.

en.title: JOINT PRESS STATEMENT - Third Senior Officials Meeting between the Maldives and the European Union
en.description: Third Senior Officials Meeting between the Maldives and the European Union
en.body:
Third Senior Officials Meeting between the Maldives and the European Union

The Third Senior Officials Meeting between the Maldives and the European Union (EU) was held on 25 October 2022 in Malé, Maldives.

This meeting re-affirmed the positive and growing momentum in the relations between the two sides over the past years. The Maldives and European Union re-confirmed their strong mutual interest in further strengthening their bilateral relations, rooted in shared values and commitments, the principles of the UN Charter and international law, and to further deepening the engagement, including through the implementation of the EU Strategy for cooperation in the Indo-Pacific.

The EU commended the positive contributions made by Abdulla Shahid, Minister of Foreign Affairs of Maldives in his capacity as the President of the 76th Session of the United Nations General Assembly and congratulated him for the successful completion of his term.

The EU welcomed the Government of Maldives’ commitment towards consolidation of democratic governance, strengthening the rule of law and fighting corruption, promotion and protection of human rights and implementing reforms in the justice sector. The EU re-affirmed its continuous strong support to the Maldives’ endeavours, and importance for these reforms to be implemented.

As close partners in the multilateral domain, both Maldives and EU reiterated their intention to expand the existing partnership and work closely in the UN and all relevant multilateral fora, including to address global challenges such as peace and security, climate change and biodiversity, water and plastic pollution.

The EU congratulated the Maldives on being elected to the UN Human Rights Council for the term 2023-2025 and expressed hope for strong cooperation in the promotion and protection of human rights in the multilateral framework.

The Maldives and EU underlined the importance attached to the freedom of expression and opinion as essential foundations for democracy and the rule of law. The Maldives and EU also highlighted their continued strong support to civil society.

The Maldives welcomed EU’s Multi-Annual Indicative Programme (MIP) for the Maldives 2021-2027, the first dedicated envelope to the Maldives since 2013. With EUR 12 million (MVR 178.6 million) allocated for the period 2021-2024 under the MIP, both the Maldives and EU agreed to deepen cooperation in green transition, climate change mitigation and adaptation, biodiversity protection and circular economy, and continued support for good governance, rule of law and security.

Through the MIP, the Maldives would receive support from the EU in key areas of the Strategic Action Plan 2019-2023 and the National Resilience and Recovery Plan. The Maldives especially welcomed EU’s new actions for judiciary reforms and biodiversity protection.

The Maldives and EU concurred on the need to enhance security cooperation especially in areas of counterterrorism and preventing violent extremism and agreed to explore avenues and expand the partnership, including through a new project focused on increasing security in the Maldives.

As partners in trade and investment, both the Maldives and EU agreed to enhance economic cooperation through mechanisms such as the Business Roundtable initiative.

The EU and the Maldives are committed to the global fight against illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing and look forward to strengthening their bilateral partnership in this domain. Sustainable management of fish stocks through the Indian Ocean Tuna Commission was discussed.

The Government of the Maldives reiterated its request to the EU to consider granting duty free access for sustainably sourced tuna products from the Maldives. Recalling the importance of enhancing people-to-people ties between the two sides, the Maldives also reiterated its request for visa free travel for Maldivian nationals to travel to EU Member states.

The Third Senior Officials Meeting between the Maldives and EU was held in a hybrid format with the discussions co-chaired by Ahmed Khaleel, Minister of State for Foreign Affairs and Paola Pampaloni, Deputy Managing Director for Asia and Pacific at the European External Action Service.

en.title: Message from His Excellency Abdulla Shahid, Minister of Foreign Affairs, on the occasion of the UN Day
en.description: Message from His Excellency Abdulla Shahid, Minister of Foreign Affairs, on the occasion of the UN Day
en.body:
Message from His Excellency Abdulla Shahid, Minister of Foreign Affairs, on the occasion of the UN Day

“Today, we mark the seventy-seventh anniversary of the entry into force of the United Nations Charter; the Charter that has guided this most universal body of nations for over 7 decades.   The United Nations continues to stand as a steadfast symbol of hope for a better world and to deliver a prosperous future we want; a symbol of hope for global unity for peace, development, human rights, and equal opportunity and prosperity for all.    The Maldives, reiterates its steadfast commitment to the principles of the UN Charter and its values of peace, justice, respect, human rights, tolerance, and solidarity. We celebrate this day with our unwavering commitment to the purposes and principles of the UN Charter, multilateralism, diplomacy, and our commitment to further strengthening its partnership with the United Nations.   We celebrate the important work the United Nations has carried out across the world in the past seven decades. The 2030 Agenda and the Sustainable Development Goals is a testament to the UN’s efforts to make a difference in the lives of everyone around the world. It is also the most successful anti-poverty campaign ever and will require unprecedented international cooperation and innovative approaches to achieve all the 17 SDGs for a more equal, just, and sustainable world for all.    Today, the United Nations is facing challenges like never before. This is the time to recommit to the United Nations, its Charter and its values. This is the time to adopt a holistic approach to address global problems including the recognition of identifying the different needs of different countries and the need for different responses. This is the time for collective global action to tackle climate change, promote gender equality, and address the myriad of global problems that face us all. This is the time to amplify our shared interests in preventing conflict and maintaining peace and stability – solidarity and resilience across the world.   Today, the Maldives renews its commitment to the United Nations, and our hope and conviction that it remains the most legitimate global platform to serve humanity, and to protect the sanctity of human life”.

en.title: The Maldives Wins a Seat at the UN Human Rights Council
en.description: The Maldives Wins a Seat at the UN Human Rights Council
en.body:
The Maldives Wins a Seat at the UN Human Rights Council

The Maldives has won a seat at the United Nations Human Rights Council, at the elections held today at the United Nations General Assembly in New York today.

Today’s election saw 17 countries competing for 14 vacant seats. The Maldives competed in the Group of Asia-Pacific States, for one of the 4 vacant seats.

The Maldives won with 154 votes, out of a total of 189 votes cast. Along with the Maldives, Bangladesh, Vietnam, and Kyrgyzstan also won seats for the Group of Asia-Pacific States.

The membership for the UN Humans Rights Council is based on equitable geographical distribution, and seats are allotted as follows among regional groups:

Group of African States (13)
Group of Asia-Pacific States (13)
Group of Eastern European States (6)
Group of Latin American and Caribbean States (8)
Group of Western European and other States (7)
The 47 members at the United Nations Human Rights Council not only reflects the United Nation’s diversity, but it gives the Council legitimacy when speaking out on human rights violations in all countries.

Members serve for a period of three years and are not eligible for immediate re-election after serving two consecutive terms. The new members will start their terms on January 1, 2023.
